A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the age-related loss in synaptic number and synaptic function (synaptophysin) may be due to the loss in glial (astroglial) support of synapses, and that the FGL peptide may act to'restore' this support.

the age-related loss in synapses and glia-synaptic interaction may be attenuated by FGL, and that the effects of this peptide on glial-synthesis interaction may be mediated through regulation of CD200.
the age-related decrease in CD200 expression, together with a reduction in the number of astrocyte-sympatctic interactions, may contribute to the age-related loss in synaptophysin expression.
The main takeaway from our work is that
FGL may exert its neuroprotective action by modulating glial-synapse interactions, and that these effects may involve the modulation of CD200 expression.
FGL peptide treatment may have a beneficial effect on synaptic integrity in aging by regulating glial cell activity and/or by maintaining the integrity of glial-synapse interactions.
FGL treatment may be useful as a therapeutic agent to counteract the age-related loss in synaptic plasticity, which is a key feature in age-associated memory impairment.
